appraisal_events.evidence: "elle se mit à me faire sur sa famille des reproches qui me semblèrent du reste fort justes, et auxquels Saint-Loup...adhéra entièrement"; the narrator, sensing "la bonne influence de sa maîtresse", was ready to advise Saint-Loup to send his family away.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator validates Rachel's judgment of Saint-Loup's family as fair, and Saint-Loup submits to it entirely, giving her clear emotional authority over him that the narrator himself endorses.

appraisal_events.evidence: "Et croyez-vous que la mère de Robert, une femme pieuse, dit qu'il faut qu'il reste à l'île du Diable, même s'il est innocent? n'est-ce pas une horreur?"
appraisal_events.explanation: Rachel indicts Mme de Marsantes's pious rigidity as monstrous even toward a man she believes may be innocent, and the surrounding sympathetic framing of Rachel's grief does not undercut the charge.

status_effects.explanation: Rachel's view of Saint-Loup's family prevails, and Saint-Loup adheres to it entirely, giving her clear leverage that the narrator himself credits as a good influence.
Saint-Loup submits entirely to Rachel's judgment even on family matters, underscoring his dependence on her.
Her insistence that Dreyfus remain imprisoned even if innocent is called a horror, discrediting her moral standing in this local exchange.
